title: gevent Timer.cancel() fails to stop recurring callbacks after the first tick
author: IsaacsonMango
body_preview: ## Description  When using Celery's `gevent` pool (`-P gevent`), cancelling a periodic timer created by `Timer.call_repeatedly()` fails once the first callback has completed. title: Memory queue purges can race with consumers and raise IndexError
author: IlyaKhalafi
body_preview: The memory transport counts messages through `Queue.qsize()` and then clears `Queue.queue` outside the queue mutex. A consumer can acquire the mutex after the count, find a message, and reach `deque.popleft()` after the purge removes it. This raises `IndexError` instead of returning a message or `queue.Empty`. title: filesystem transport: queue_unbind does not update the exchange file, so unbound queues keep receiving messages
author: moneebullah25
body_preview: On the `filesystem://` transport, `Channel.queue_unbind` does not persist the removal of a binding. The in-memory `state.binding_delete` does run, so only the exchange file on disk is stale. The binding stays in the exchange file, so later direct/fanout publishes (including from other processes) are still routed to the unbound queue. title: RQ cron scheduler does not respect Django TIME_ZONE
author: chromium7
body_preview: ## Summary  Cron expressions registered through `django_rq` are evaluated in UTC instead of the timezone configured in Django's `TIME_ZONE`.
